sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by confocal microscopy and flow cytometry in HEK293 cells. Electrophysiological function not explicitly reported for the BBS-tagged construct in the cited papers, but robust surface trafficking was demonstrated. Multiple independent studies using HA tags in the same S1–S2 loop (same protein, same loop) report no interference with processing or function (Akhavan et al. 2003, cited in PMC3861077).
sites.rationale: The ledger explicitly names T436/E437 as the insertion junction in the extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology landmarks: EC 430–453, flanked by TM S1 409–429 and TM S2 454–471). Python verification confirms full_seq[436]='T' and full_seq[437]='E', matching the paper exactly. Distance from S1 TM end (429): 7 residues; distance from S2 TM start (454): 18 residues — both well above the ≥3 residue minimum. The nearest disulfide-forming cysteines (C445, C449) are 9 and 13 residues downstream, respectively, leaving adequate spacing. The BBS tag (13 aa) is within the 13–23 aa target range; an ALFA tag with GS linkers (~19–21 aa) is similarly sized. Multiple independent papers confirm this loop tolerates epitope insertions without disrupting trafficking. A 13-residue bungarotoxin-binding site (BBS) was inserted between T436 and E437 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop of full-length hERG1a (also bearing a C-terminal YFP) in HEK293 cells. Surface expression of the intact membrane-anchored channel was confirmed by confocal microscopy (YFP total pool; BTX-Alexa647 surface pool) and flow cytometry (surface signals up to 100-fold above threshold). The construct is full-length and membrane-anchored; not a secreted ectodomain. [validation: surface_only; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: A 13-residue bungarotoxin-binding site (BBS; TGGCGGTACTACGAGAGCAGCCTGGAGCCCTACCCCGAC) ( Sekine-Aizawa and Huganir, 2004 ; Yang et al., 2010 ) was then introduced between residues T436/E437 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop of hERG using the Quik-Change Lightning Site-Directed Mutagenesis Kit (Stratagene) according to the manufacturer's instructions. 16 LQT2 mutations were introduced in the PAS domain of BBS-hERG-YFP via site-directed mutagenesis.

sites.rationale: The ledger explicitly names T443/E444 as the insertion junction in the extracellular S1–S2 loop. Python verification confirms full_seq[443]='T' and full_seq[444]='E', matching the paper exactly. Distance from S1 TM end (429): 14 residues; distance from S2 TM start (454): 11 residues — both well above the ≥3 residue minimum. C445 is 2 residues downstream of the junction; however, the paper explicitly demonstrates electrophysiological function is preserved, indicating the insert does not disrupt the C445–C449 disulfide. The HA-with-linkers insert (17 aa) is within the 13–23 aa target range; an ALFA tag with GS linkers is similarly sized. A second ledger line (PMC7704534) independently confirms HA tagging in the first extracellular loop of KV11.1/KCNH2 with surface expression validated by flow cytometry and confocal microscopy. A 9-amino acid HA tag with flanking 4-aa linkers (NSEHYPYDVPDYAVTFE, 17 aa total) was inserted between T443 and E444 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop of full-length KCNH2 (hERG1a) by inverse PCR. The construct was incorporated into a stable expression system (AttB-KCNH2-HA:IRES:mCherry). The paper explicitly states the tag does not affect electrophysiological properties of the channel. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: A previously published 34 9 amino acid HA tag with surrounding 4 amino acid linkers (NSEHYPYDVPDYAVTFE) was inserted between amino acids T443 and E444 (in the extracellular region between the S1 and S2 helices) by inverse PCR 35 (Table S1).

literature_notes: Two validated sites were identified, both in the extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology 430–453) of KCNH2. All other ledger entries were considered: (1) Multiple corroborating HA-in-S1S2-loop entries (PMC3861077, PMC3877390, PMC7704534, PMC13182972, PMC5917007) do not add new residue-level positions beyond 436 and 443 — they confirm the loop tolerates insertions and support both sites as additional corroboration. (2) The N-terminal myc tag and C-terminal myc tag (PMC5671924) are both intracellular (N-terminus 1–408 is intracellular; C-terminus 657–1159 is intracellular per topology landmarks) and do not qualify as extracellular sites. (3) The BBS surface-labeling confocal and flow cytometry entries (PMC5917007, three additional quotes) are corroborating evidence for site 1 at 436, not independent new sites. (4) The large extracellular S5–S6 loop (571–638) contains no ledger-grounded insertion at a specific residue and was therefore not proposed. Site 1 (436) is ranked higher because the BBS tag size (13 aa) is the closest match to the ALFA tag target range and the site is farther from the C445–C449 disulfide pair; Site 2 (443) is ranked second because function was explicitly confirmed by electrophysiology, giving it 'surface_and_function' validation, but proximity to C445 (2 residues) is a structural note.
